query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)** (October 2026). **Closest match:** a meta-agent diagnoses training failures and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and RL configuration during ongoing multi-turn RL, with validated changes applied live. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04785)** (April 2025). 3. **[Meta-Agent: Continual Learning for Agents](https://github.com/canvas-org/meta-agent)** (2026). Related system that uses execution traces to modify prompts, tools, control flow, and other agent infrastructure while keeping model weights frozen. **Person:** Essam Sleiman (Canvas). Relevant to meta-agent modification, though it does not perform multi-turn reinforcement learning.

text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — Studies how turn-level rewards and trajectory scoring affect LLM agents trained against simulated users. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

2. **[Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13617)** — Simulators generate user reactions and per-turn ratings that serve directly as rewards for multi-turn assistant training. **People:** Tarek Naous (Google Research and Georgia Tech), Craig Boutilier and Ofer Meshi (Google Research), Wei Xu (Georgia Tech).

3. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336)** — Trains simulators with an LLM judge’s reward for responses indistinguishable from real users, rather than matching a single reference response. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations represented:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab.

4. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02208)** — Introduces UserVille’s preference-aware user simulators and rewards combining task success, clarification quality, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang (Carnegie Mellon University); Xingyao Wang (OpenHands).
